subject: Pilot candidate model slate — conclusion, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodai.com>
To: Michael Barnes <mbarnes@novusai.com>, Elaine Chu <elaine@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot candidate model slate — conclusion, benchmarks, and next steps

Hi Michael / Elaine,

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday — appreciate the candid feedback on the multi-turn summarization flows and the low-latency inference needs for your mobile agents. Per our agreement on the call, I pulled together a concise candidate slate with practical tradeoffs and the artifacts you asked for. Quick TL;DR first: three candidates, recommended default, and a safety fallback.

Recommended candidates (shortlist):
- Redwood-Moderate-13B-q4_8bit — Best overall quality/latency balance for your 1–2s SLO on 512-token contexts. Strong on instruction-following and summarization.
- OpenHawk-7B-int8 — Lowest cost baseline with decent latency; expect small regressions on edge-case factual recall in long dialogs.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B-v2 — High throughput, very good quality for instruction tasks, but slightly higher memory; good for batch inferencing and rerank.

Fallback: Redwood-XL-3B-quant — cheap, ultra-low-latency fallback for burst traffic and degraded capacity.

Attached: novus_benchmarks_20280425.csv (latency P50/P95, cost/token estimates), prompt-sets-novus-v1.json (canonical prompt pack & acceptance test set), and the demo recording. Benchmarks summary:
- Redwood-Moderate-13B-q4_8bit: P50 ~ 420ms, P95 ~ 1.7s (on g5.2x-sized instance pool), est cost ~$140 / 1M tokens.
- OpenHawk-7B-int8: P50 ~ 230ms, P95 ~ 900ms, est cost ~$45 / 1M tokens.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B-v2: P50 ~ 360ms, P95 ~ 1.2s, est cost ~$80 / 1M tokens.

Operational notes and quality/regression considerations:
- We recommend running Redwood-Moderate-13B as the pilot default with OpenHawk as a low-cost A/B cohort (10–15% traffic) to validate acceptance tests.
- Prompt-set v1 includes 120 seed examples focusing on multi-turn coherence, hallucination stress tests, and extraction accuracy. Please run these on your side — the acceptance bar is in the header of the JSON.
- We flagged three prompt families where quantized 7B variants exhibit a 5–8% drop in factual extraction F1; Ben included model-level details below.

Proposed next steps (owners & timing):
1) Your team: run the prompt-set v1 against OpenHawk + Redwood-Moderate (ETA: 3 business days).
2) Redwood (Ben): upload per-model latency/cost breakdown and a short guide to canary rollout (ETA: 48 hours).
3) Redwood (Kimberly): draft pilot SOW and canary runbook (ETA: 5 business days).
4) Sync call to finalize pilot metrics and procurement path (suggest Tue 04/30).

If that roadmap looks good, I’ll loop in procurement and schedule the 04/30 sync.

Thanks —
Avery

Thanks Avery — super helpful summary and clear asks. Two quick clarifying questions before we kick off the prompt runs: 

1) Latency SLO: our mobile agent requires end-to-end P95 <= 1.2s for interactive sessions (includes network + infra). Can you confirm the P95 numbers you shared include only server-side inference, and if so, any suggestions to hit 1.2s end-to-end?

2) Quality/regressions: you mentioned a 5–8% drop in factual extraction F1 on quantized 7B variants. For our critical extraction flows (4 seed templates), what would you recommend as a guardrail in production to catch regressions early?

I’ll have procurement standing by once we lock on the pilot SOW and cost estimate.

-Michael

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Michael Barnes <mbarnes@novusai.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot candidate model slate — conclusion, benchmarks, and next steps

Hi Michael — quick answers to your questions with concrete numbers and guardrails.

1) Latency: the CSV and linked report are server-side inference only. Network + client overhead typically adds ~120–300ms depending on region and mobile carrier. To target 1.2s end-to-end P95 we suggest:
   - Use Redwood-Moderate-13B-q4_8bit on our dedicated pool in us-west with a colocated edge (adds ~80ms). Expected server-side P95 ~1.1–1.3s depending on bursts.
   - Enable continuous batching with a max_wait of 30ms and size cap of 16; this reduces cost without materially impacting P95 in low-concurrency mobile traffic.

2) Regression guardrails: recommended lightweight pipeline:
   - Canary: route 5% traffic to candidate with full logging and shadow inference for another 15% to compare outputs.
   - Ongoing checks: run the 120 acceptance examples every 4 hours; fail the canary if extraction F1 drops >3% vs baseline.
   - Runtime heuristic: if extraction confidence < 0.7 for any critical field, mark for human review and route to fallback OpenHawk-7B-int8 for that request.

3) Cost sensitivity note: per our internal calc (see CSV) running Redwood-Moderate-13B as default with a 10% OpenHawk cohort yields a blended cost ~20–25% lower than Redwood-only, with monitoring overhead.

I attached the CSV with per-model sample runs and a simple cost calculator tab. Happy to walk through the numbers on the sync.

-Ben

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodai.com>

Michael / team — putting the ops checklist and owners inline so we have clear actionables for the pilot kickoff.

Pilot runbook (high level):
- Scope: 2-week pilot, 1 production-like endpoint, 10% A/B cohort to OpenHawk, 5% canary window for Redwood-Moderate.
- Metrics: P50/P95 latency, extraction F1 on the acceptance set, end-to-end success rate, and cost per 1k requests.
- Rollout plan:
  * Day 0 (kickoff): baseline runs on your staging traffic (Avery) + smoke tests (Novus).
  * Day 1–3: run acceptance batch; stabilize telemetry; iterate prompt tweaks (Karthik owner).
  * Day 4–7: canary ramp to 5%; enable shadowing at 20% for top queries.
  * Day 8–14: evaluate and decide conversion to Redwood-Moderate or widen OpenHawk cohort.
- Monitoring & alerting: set up an automated job to compute extraction F1 every 4 hours and an alert if drop >3% for 2 consecutive windows.

Please confirm the proposed kickoff on Tue 04/30 9:00 AM PT (we'll put a 30-min slot). Also confirm who from your team will run the acceptance pack and who owns the procurement review so we can loop them in.

Thanks,
Kimberly
